payload.title: Multi-Cloud Reference Architecture
payload.content:
# Technical Specification — Multi-Cloud Reference Architecture

## Architecture
Event-driven microservices on Kubernetes. All services expose gRPC internally
and REST/JSON externally. Schema registry enforces contract compatibility.

## Technology Stack
MLOps pipelines (Kubeflow/MLflow), developer experience AI (Copilot-class code intelligence), observability stack (OpenTelemetry + PromQL), and policy-as-code governance

## Data Architecture
**Primary:** PostgreSQL 16 (application data) + ClickHouse (analytics/telemetry) + Redis Cluster (rate limiting/caching)
**Cache:** Redis Cluster (read-through, write-behind)
**Search:** Elasticsearch 8 (BM25 + kNN hybrid)
**Streaming:** Apache Kafka (3-node, RF=3, ISR=2)

## Security Controls
| Control | Implementation |
|---------|----------------|
| AuthN | OAuth 2.0 + OIDC (RS256 JWT) |
| AuthZ | RBAC + ABAC via OPA Gatekeeper |
| Encryption at rest | AES-256-GCM (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) |
| Encryption in transit | TLS 1.3 (mTLS service-to-service) |
| Secrets management | HashiCorp Vault (dynamic credentials) |
| Vulnerability scanning | Trivy (container) + Dependabot (deps) |

## Scalability Targets
- Throughput: 50,000 req/min sustained
- Latency: p50 ≤ 80ms · p95 ≤ 150ms · p99 ≤ 200ms
- Availability: 99.95% monthly SLA
- Storage: petabyte-scale object storage for model artefacts

## CI/CD Pipeline
GitHub Actions → unit tests → integration tests → container build →
SAST/DAST scan → staging deploy → smoke tests → production canary (5% → 100%)

---

structured.title: Multi-Cloud Reference Architecture
structured.goal: For the Enterprise Architect, the goal is to validate the proposed multi-cloud strategy as technically sound, strategically aligned with business objectives, and capable of addressing current AI/ML limitations. Success means securing architectural approval for the phased adoption and hyperscaler selection framework.
structured.blueprintContext:
This assessment defines a future-ready multi-cloud strategy to complement the client's existing Azure estate, addressing limitations in specialized compute, scalability, and service diversity for AI/ML and data-intensive workloads. The objective is achievable by strategically integrating a secondary hyperscaler (AWS or GCP) to access differentiated AI/ML capabilities and improve workload portability, while maintaining robust governance. The headline recommendation is to proceed with a phased multi-cloud adoption, prioritizing either AWS or GCP based on a structured evaluation framework, with an initial focus on AI/ML pilot use cases.

## Current State Assessment Summary
The client possesses a mature Azure Landing Zone with strong centralized governance and platform engineering. However, this single-hyperscaler approach exhibits structural limitations for evolving AI/ML and data-intensive workloads, particularly regarding specialized compute, scalability, and service diversity. Multi-region Azure mitigation has not fully resolved these constraints, indicating a need for broader hyperscaler capabilities [S1].

## Target Multi-Cloud Architecture & Strategy
The target architecture will integrate Azure with a secondary hyperscaler (AWS or GCP) to leverage differentiated AI/ML capabilities and specialized services. A workload placement strategy will guide decisions on where to host specific AI/ML and data platforms, optimizing for performance, cost, and access to unique features. I

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.body:
Event-driven microservices on Kubernetes. All services expose gRPC internally
and REST/JSON externally. Schema registry enforces contract compatibility.

sections.heading: Technology Stack
sections.body: MLOps pipelines (Kubeflow/MLflow), developer experience AI (Copilot-class code intelligence), observability stack (OpenTelemetry + PromQL), and policy-as-code governance

sections.heading: Data Architecture
sections.body:
**Primary:** PostgreSQL 16 (application data) + ClickHouse (analytics/telemetry) + Redis Cluster (rate limiting/caching)
**Cache:** Redis Cluster (read-through, write-behind)
**Search:** Elasticsearch 8 (BM25 + kNN hybrid)
**Streaming:** Apache Kafka (3-node, RF=3, ISR=2)

sections.heading: Security Controls
sections.body:
| Control | Implementation |
|---------|----------------|
| AuthN | OAuth 2.0 + OIDC (RS256 JWT) |
| AuthZ | RBAC + ABAC via OPA Gatekeeper |
| Encryption at rest | AES-256-GCM (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) |
| Encryption in transit | TLS 1.3 (mTLS service-to-service) |
| Secrets management | HashiCorp Vault (dynamic credentials) |
| Vulnerability scanning | Trivy (container) + Dependabot (deps) |

sections.heading: Scalability Targets
sections.body:
- Throughput: 50,000 req/min sustained
- Latency: p50 ≤ 80ms · p95 ≤ 150ms · p99 ≤ 200ms
- Availability: 99.95% monthly SLA
- Storage: petabyte-scale object storage for model artefacts

sections.heading: CI/CD Pipeline
sections.body:
GitHub Actions → unit tests → integration tests → container build →
SAST/DAST scan → staging deploy → smoke tests → production canary (5% → 100%)

---
